material.text: g3saranath/opencode-pet: A desktop pet for opencode that scries your session and scribes it live — a wizard on a broom streaming reasoning, tool calls, and output.
type=plugin source=github:g3saranath/opencode-pet created=2026-08-13T18:57:04Z firstSeen=2026-11-05T11:00:42.618Z published=? maintainers=? repoId=1333445869 stars=1 npm30d=?

# Opencode Scrybe Pet **A desktop pet for [opencode](https://opencode.ai) that _scries_ your session and _scribes_ it live.** A little wizard on a broom perches on top of your screen and shows what your agent is doing, in real time - streaming reasoning and replies, every tool call and its output, plans, permissions, and the final result. He reacts as work happens and dozes off when opencode isn't running.
## Modes The character itself changes with the work - not just a badge on top.
idle
calm hover		 thinking
eyes up, pondering		 working
heads-down + live action		 sleeping
opencode disconnected
## Features - **Live relay.** A transcript panel streams the session as it happens - your prompt, the model's **reasoning** and **response** (streaming, updating in place), each tool call with its target, and the tool **output**. - **Live status bubble.** The current action + target at a glance: `✏️ token.ts`, `⚙️ testing`, `🔍 TODO`, `📝 3/5 done`, `❓ allow shell npm test?`. Shell commands get short labels (`npm test` → testing, `git commit` → committing, `gh pr edit` → editing PR) while the log keeps the real command, and with nothing specific to show he cycles through wizard verbs (casting, conjuring, scrying, …). - **Custom per-mode art.** Distinct artwork for thinking, working, and sleeping, with a mood colour-grade and its own flight motion. - **Auto wake / sleep.** Follows the desktop app, not the background service. The pet appears when you open the app, vanishes when you close it, and comes back when you reopen it. Automatic on Windows; on macOS and Linux it needs `OPENCODE_PET_APP_PROCESS` (see [Platform](#platform)), otherwise the pet stays awake while opencode runs. The stale-heartbeat timeout is only the fallback if the plugin cannot close it first. - **Stays put & draggable.** Sits where you leave him; drag to reposition (remembered across restarts). - **Sound, sizing, and a right-click menu.** Completion chime (mutable), four sizes, toggle the log, reset position, quit. ## How it works ``` opencode ──(plugin)──► ~/.cache/opencode-pet/state.json ──(watch)──► Electron overlay ``` - **`plugin/pet.ts`** - an opencode plugin (Node built-ins plus this repo's `shared/` modules). It hooks into session / tool / message events, keeps a rolling relay of the recent steps and the streaming reasoning/response, and writes it (throttled) to a small state file. While the desktop app is open it pulses a heartbeat and launches the overlay; when the app closes it deletes the heartbeat and closes the pet. - **`app/`** - a transparent, always-on-top Electron window. The character is a raster sprite animated with CSS; each mood swaps the sprite and layers motion, a colour-grade, and overlays. Click-through everywhere except the character. The overlay and plugin talk only through files in `~/.cache/opencode-pet/`, so there are no ports and nothing to configure. ## Install Requires [opencode](https://opencode.ai) **2.x** and [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 22.18 or newer. The plugin uses the V2 plugin contract, so OpenCode 1 will not load it. ```sh git clone https://github.com/g3saranath/opencode-pet.git ~/opencode-pet cd ~/opencode-pet npm install # downloads Electron ``` > `npm install` fetches the Electron app through this project's `postinstall` > script. If you install with `--ignore-scripts`, Electron downloads itself the > first time the overlay starts instead. Then register the plugin with opencode by adding its absolute path to `plugins` in your global config, `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` (create the file if it doesn't exist): ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugins": ["/Users/you/opencode-pet/plugin/pet.ts"], } ``` On Windows, use a `file://` URL with forward slashes, for example `"file:///D:/Projects/opencode-pet/plugin/pet.ts"`. Then **restart opencode** (or run `opencode service restart`). Scrybe appears automatically and starts relaying the session. > **Point at the clone, don't copy.** `plugin/pet.ts` imports this repo's > `shared/` modules, so the config entry must point at the file inside your > clone. Copying `pet.ts` on its own into `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` will > fail to load. > Prefer not to auto-launch the overlay? Set `OPENCODE_PET_NO_LAUNCH=1` and > run it yourself with `npm start`. ## Controls | Action | How | | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | | Move | Left-click and drag | | Menu | **Right-click** - Size, Mute, Activity log, Reset, Quit pet | | Resize | Right-click ▸ Size ▸ Small / Medium / Large / Huge | | Mute sounds | Right-click ▸ Mute sounds | | Show/hide log | Right-click ▸ Show activity log | | Quit | Right-click ▸ Quit pet, or `Ctrl`+`Alt`+`Shift`+`P` | | Run manually | `npm start` | ## Configuration | Variable | Effect | | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | | `OPENCODE_PET_DIR` | Path to this checkout (defaults to the checkout the plugin lives in) | | `OPENCODE_PET_NO_LAUNCH=1` | Don't auto-launch the overlay from the plugin | | `OPENCODE_PET_APP_PROCESS` | Desktop app process name to follow for wake / sleep (default `OpenCode.exe` on Windows, off elsewhere) | | `OPENCODE_PET_DEBUG=1` | Log event types the plugin doesn't handle to `debug.log` | Runtime files live in `~/.cache/opencode-pet/`: `state.json` (current relay), `heartbeat` (connection pulse), `owner.pid` (which plugin instance drives the pet), `pet.pid` (overlay pid), `pos.json` (position), `config.json` (size / mute / log preferences), and `debug.log` (only with `OPENCODE_PET_DEBUG=1`). ## For AI agents and other IDEs Built for OpenCode, but the overlay is just a file watcher. Any agent or IDE can drive the wizard by writing the same two files in `~/.cache/opencode-pet/`: - `state.json`: `{ state, feed }` where `state` is one of `idle | thinking | working | waiting | happy | error | sleeping` and `feed` is an array of `{ seq, icon, text, kind }`. See `shared/state-protocol.js` as the reference (atomic write via `state.json.tmp` rename, deduped, with `ts`). - `heartbeat`: `" "` updated every few seconds while the agent is alive. Delete it and write `state: sleeping` on shutdown so the pet naps and then quits. Minimal example (adjust the path to point at your clone): ```js const { createStateWriter } = require("/path/to/opencode-pet/shared/state-protocol"); const writeState = createStateWriter(); writeState("working", { detail: "edit token.ts" }, [{ seq: 1, icon: "\u270F\uFE0F", text: "edit token.ts", kind: "step" }]); ``` The `heartbeat` pid is used to tell whose pulse it is: the overlay checks that the process is still alive, so a crashed agent can't keep the pet awake by leaving a fresh timestamp behind. Write your own `process.pid` there. No ports or extra config. Just write the files and the wizard reacts. PRs for other adapters are welcome. ## Swapping the art The character lives in `app/renderer/` as `sprite.png` (idle / fallback) plus `sprite-thinking.png`, `sprite-working.png`, and `sprite-sleeping.png`. Each is used for its state and falls back to `sprite.png` when absent. Drop in your own square, transparent-background PNGs with the same names and restart the overlay. ## Platform Built on macOS (Apple Silicon) and also tested on Windows. It uses standard Electron overlay APIs, so Linux should work with minor tweaks - PRs welcome. The overlay runs on Electron 44, which needs macOS 13 or newer, or 64-bit Windows or Linux. Auto wake / sleep checks whether the desktop app's process is running. On Windows it looks for `OpenCode.exe` out of the box. On macOS and Linux, set `OPENCODE_PET_APP_PROCESS` to the app's exact process name (matched with `pgrep -x`) to turn it on. Without it, the pet stays awake while opencode runs and won't vanish when you close the app. That's also the right setting if you only use the terminal client, since there is no desktop process to follow. If the plugin can't close the pet itself, the overlay naps about 45 seconds after the last heartbeat and quits 15 seconds after that. ## Contributing Issues and PRs are welcome. The code is deliberately small and dependency-light (one Electron dependency for the app; the plugin uses only Node built-ins plus this repo's `shared/` modules - no npm packages at runtime). Run `npm test` before sending a PR. ## License [MIT](LICENSE) © g3saranath ## Notice The bundled character art is fan art of a well-known wizard-on-a-broom character. This project is **not affiliated with, endorsed by, or associated with** Warner Bros., J.K. Rowling, or the Harry Potter franchise, and is shared for non-commercial, personal use only.
